newsitem.title: FINLAND: LITHUANIA-SWISS UBS SAYS SHARES SET TO RISE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-SWISS UBS SAYS SHARES SET TO RISE.

text.p: Swiss bank giant Union Banque Suisse (UBS) views Lithuanian shares as set for gains in the future as they are under-valued compared with Estonia and Latvia.
UBS eastern and central Europe equities director James Oates said investors were looking for positive signals and real change from the new government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius.

"It (Lithuanian shares) is clearly due for a run if we see some signs of genuine change that will make Lithuania interesting," he told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday at an investment conference in the Finnish capital.
All Baltic stock exchanges soared higher in January but Estonia has maintained a positive run recently.
Many analysts now say that Estonia is over-valued whereas Lithuania is cheap and has been lagging both Estonia and Latvia.
"We could expect an evening up of performance: on the one hand, Lithuania going up and the other two stagnating," Oates added.
He said that price/earnings ratios seemed cheap compared with Estonia and Latvia.
"Unless something dreadful happens, I would expect to see the market rising back," Oates added.
